title: Schema-Guard Log Gateway: resilient structured log normalization with session affinity and backpressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current log pipeline is brittle for polyglot structured inputs coming from edge services and SDKs. Field names vary by language/SDK versions, timestamps are inconsistent, and tenant-specific PII scrubbing is applied inconsistently at the source. This causes noisy alerts, misattributed traces, and high downstream storage costs when unstructured fallbacks are used.

Goal: Build a resilient, lightweight gateway (Schema-Guard) that normalizes structured log envelopes at the network boundary, performs deterministic field mapping and redaction, attaches stable session fingerprints, and exposes per-tenant backpressure signals to upstream SDKs/sidecars. The gateway must preserve ordering within a session, tolerate short-term spikes without dropping important events, and emit observability metrics that let Console drive routing/fallback decisions.

Non-goals: Full semantic parsing or expensive enrichment (these remain separate services). Gateway should not be a long-term store — only transient buffering and transformation.

Constraints and design principles: resilient-by-default, tenant isolation (soft quotas, per-tenant circuit-breakers), minimal CPU overhead (avoid heavy JSON parsing where possible), deterministic mappings (same input -> same canonical envelope), and safe-by-default redaction (configurable allow-list for fields).
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts JSON/JSONL envelopes over HTTP and gRPC and returns 2xx only after normalization and tenant-scoped policy checks.

Canonical schema: timestamps normalized to RFC3339, message -> message.text, level normalized to canonical set {DEBUG,INFO,WARN,ERROR}, and any unknown top-level fields moved under metadata.raw_{orig_field}.
Session fingerprint added for session affinity: deterministic 64-bit fingerprint derived from configured keys (user_id, session_id, client_nonce) and stable salt per-tenant.
Per-tenant backpressure: gateway exposes short-lived 202 responses with Retry-After when tenant budget or queue high; Console shows real-time queued events and headroom metrics.
Redaction: PII patterns (email, credit_card_like, ssn_like) removed by default; customers can configure additional allow-list fields via Console or API.
End-to-end integration tests validate order preservation for same-session streams and dropping of malformed envelopes does not break downstream indexer consumers.
Latency SLO: p50 < 10ms, p95 < 40ms for in-path normalization under steady-state load (measured in our perf harness).
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): HTTP/gRPC ingress, minimal JSONPath-driven canonicalizer, deterministic fingerprint routine, in-memory per-tenant ring buffer with eviction policy, basic metrics (queue_length, drop_rate, processing_latency).

Phase 2: pluggable adapters for binary/compact encodings, Circuit Breaker REST API to expose tenant state, integration with Console for realtime headroom visualization and per-tenant config overrides.
Use a streaming JSON parser (simdjson or equivalent) to avoid full document allocations for large payloads. Keep canonicalizer rules declarative (YAML) and versioned in S3/Config Service.

Backpressure semantics: for soft-high water mark signal to SDKs return 202 + Retry-After; at hard limit respond 429 and increment audit counter. Metrics emitted to metrics pipeline with tenant tags for dashboards.
Redaction pipeline: run lightweight token pattern matcher first, then field allow-list check. Avoid unbounded regex evaluations; compile regexes per-worker at startup.
Deployment: start as edge sidecar in staging-perf with 10% of traffic, feature-flag Schema-Guard canonicalization for a selected set of tenants before broad roll-out.

Observability hooks: emit trace join tag (schema_guard.version) to correlate with runtime traces; instrument batching and stall durations to Console rollouts to allow automatic fallback routing if p95 latency regresses >50%.
